title: Cognitive Load Balance Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Cognitive Load Theory
Intrinsic Load
Extraneous Load
Germane Load
MicroSim Design
description: A p5.js lab in which learners toggle design features on a mock bouncing-ball MicroSim and see a stacked load gauge split into intrinsic, extraneous and germane segments against a comfortable-capacity line, with Designer A and Designer B presets from the Chapter 3 worked example. The weights are fixed teaching illustrations, not measurements.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers and learning-technology developers

educational.topic: Intrinsic, extraneous and germane load in MicroSim design
learningObjectives: Differentiate the design features that add intrinsic, extraneous and germane load.
Identify the largest extraneous contributor to remove when a design exceeds comfortable capacity.

assumptions: Loads add; weights are made up for teaching and do not measure any learner.
limitations: Real cognitive load depends on the learner's prior knowledge and cannot be read from a MicroSim's features alone.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, toggle and observe; repair an overloaded design
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Comparison tool with feature toggles and a gauge
keyQuestions: Which segment does each feature grow, and why?
Why remove extraneous load before reducing germane load?
commonMisconceptions: All load is bad and should be minimized.
More variables always make a simulation more educational.
Decorative effects are free because AI makes them cheap to generate.
assessmentOpportunities: Classification of the six features by load type.
A minimal repair of Designer B with written reasons.
